label: input token w at original position >= 5
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter w during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 5 or later (positions 5-8, so only for L >= 6). Never fires on w at positions 0-4, on any other token, on the delimiter, or during the copy phase. Magnitude increases with position: weak at t=5 (about 0.1-0.3 of max, 8% of mass despite 40% of activations), around 0.4-0.5 of max at t=6, and strongest at t=7-8; top activations (~1.0 of max) are w as the final original token (t=8, L=9, to_go=0). Preceding tokens and sequence content have no visible effect.

issues: None of the 342 test-split false positives fall outside t=5. The feature is active on 97% of w-at-t=5 steps (t==5 predicate precision 0.970), so the misses look like near-threshold dropouts of an already weak activation, not a separate class. Narrowing to t>=6 or splitting t=5 by L does not help: t==5&L==6 still has precision 0.968.
No missed activations on the test split: recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0. The dev profile confirms zero activation in the delimiter and copy phases, zero on any token other than w, and zero at t<=4.

The magnitude claims hold. Mass share per active step goes from 0.08 over 10.7k steps at t=5, to 0.346 over 8.2k at t=6, 0.357 over 5.4k at t=7 and 0.218 over 2.8k at t=8, so mean activation rises with position. t=8 is only reachable when L=9, so 'top activations at t=8, L=9' is the same statement.
The ~seen(['w']) conjunct changes nothing (identical scores), so history has no visible effect, consistent with the explanation. The label matches the predicate.
